newsitem.title: USA: U.S. 96 agricultural exports hit record -- USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. 96 agricultural exports hit record -- USDA.

text.p: U.S. agricultural exports hit a record $60.4 billion in calendar year 1996, the U.S. Agriculture Department said Friday.
USDA said wheat exports were 31 million tonnes in 1996, down four percent from 1995. However, the value of wheat exports climbed 15 percent from the prior year to $6.2 billion due to higher prices.

Soybean exports for the year totalled 25.6 million tonnes and had a value of $7.3 billion, up 36 percent from 1995. Soybean exports to China shot up to 1.5 million tonnes in 1996 from 200,000 tonnes in 1995 and Indonesia more than doubled its imports of U.S. soybeans, taking 734,000 tonnes, USDA said.
The department said corn exports dipped 13 percent from the prior year to 52.2 million tonnes but that strong prices boosted the value of corn exports to $8.4 billion, up 15 percent over 1995.

Beef exports in 1996 were $2.4 billion, down eight percent from the prior year, and the first decline since 1977. Meanwhile, pork exports were a record $915 million, up 19 percent from 1995 and poultry reached a record $2.5 billion in 1996, USDA said.
Total U.S. agricultural imports in 1996 reached $33.6 billion, up 12 percent from 1995, the department said.
